newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gasoline pump prices fall on month - AAA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gasoline pump prices fall on month - AAA.

text.p: U.S. gasoline prices at the pump fell in the latest month, driven down by rising gasoline inventories, the American Automobile Association (AAA) said Tuesday.
A decline in crude oil prices also lowered gasoline costs, the AAA said in its monthly survey of pump prices.
The AAA said the average price of self-serve regular unleaded gasoline fell by 1.7 cents in the 30 days ending July 15, to $1.233 a gallon, or 4.1 cents below year-ago levels.
U.S. gasoline inventories totalled 204.1 million barrels as of July 4, 2.65 million barrels over last year's levels, according to the American Petroleum Institute.
Gasoline prices have been declining steadily in the past year. Nationwide, prices this month are 5.5 cents lower than at the start of the year.
Prices were lowest in the Southeast, at $1.15 a gallon -- down 2 cents in the last month and 3.9 cents lower than a year ago.
At the other extreme was the West Coast, where prices dipped about one-third of a cent and stood at a nationwide high of $1.352.
But that was still 6.7 cents lower than a year ago, when California refiners experienced a rash of serious outages that further squeezed already-tight supplies.
Light sweet crude oil futures closed Tuesday at $19.67 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange, down $2.70 a barrel from this time last year.
